title: Your own web address — how your website can get a custom domain name
body:
When it launches, your website is available at an address on our domain (for example
`yourname.citoviso.com`). On the **Web address** tab you can order **your own name** instead
(for example `yourname.com`) — this is what your guests will see, on your business card and in
Google.

We buy the name and we maintain it: you do not need to open an account with a registrar,
fiddle with DNS or deal with a certificate.

## How do I order it?

![Screenshot: the first step of the Web address tab on a phone, with the suggested names](assets/hu/screen.png)

**Step 1 — Name.** At the top of the tab you see your website's current address. Below it we offer a few
suggestions based on your business name. We check availability **directly with the
domain registrar**, at the moment you open the tab.
Next to each name is the answer:

- **Free** — anyone can buy it right now, including us; you can request this one,
- **Taken** — someone else already owns it; it cannot be requested,
- **Not available through us** — the registrar does not sell this name to us (for example because of its
  ending); choose another one,
- **Could not be checked** — the registrar did not respond just now. Until we know for sure
  that it is free, we do not offer it for purchase. Refresh the page a little later (for your own
  idea, use the **„Retry”** button).

If you do not like any of the suggestions, you can type your own into the **„Or type your own idea”**
field, and we check it with the **„Verification”** (Check) button. Feel free to type it the way you would see it in the
browser (`https://`, `www.`, capital letters) — we tidy it up ourselves and
write the cleaned-up form back into the field, so you can see what we are checking.
If something in it cannot be used, we tell you why in a simple sentence.
A so-called **premium** name — one for which the domain seller asks several times the usual
price — cannot be requested through us; if you type one, we flag it immediately
during the check, and it is worth choosing another name.
We do not offer every ending (for example `.com` is not available everywhere): if you type one
we do not offer, we tell you immediately and list the endings you can
choose from. Our suggestions also only use these endings.

The first free name is selected in advance (the dot in front of the name). If you want another one, tap
it, then the **„Next”** button below the list. If there is not a single free name on the list,
the "Next" button cannot be pressed — in that case type your own idea. If you typed your own name and
had it checked, you take it further with the **„I'd like this”** (I want this one) button in the result box.

![Screenshot: the Review step on a phone, with the steps of the reservation](assets/hu/review.png)

**Step 2 — Review.** When you get here, we check the name with the registrar once more
("Free — just checked"). Here you see in one place what you are ordering: the chosen address, the
address's **monthly fee**, the subscription term you commit to, and how much we **reserve** on your
card now. If you have changed your mind, you can choose a new name with the **„Back”** button. If everything is
fine, tap the **„Continue to payment (hold)”** (Continue to payment (reservation)) button — you reach Barion's secure
payment page.

Only **one** own-address order can run at a time. If you send the same name from two windows (or
by clicking twice), we take you back to the same payment — no second order is created,
and we do not reserve twice. While an order is running, or your address is already live, you cannot
start a new one: the tab then shows its status.

If the name is no longer free at the second check, the step has **no payment button**: the page
tells you that the name is taken or not available through us, and you can choose another one with the **„Back”**
button. If the registrar did not respond just now, you can ask again with the **„Retry”** button.
If the payment page did not open, the top of the page says: "The payment could not be
started. Please try again." — in that case we have not reserved anything.

**You only pay once the name is yours.** On the payment page the amount is **only
reserved** on your card — this is not yet a charge, the money stays in your account. Then we immediately
buy the name, and **we only charge** your card **after a successful purchase**. If the name
has been sold in the meantime, or it cannot be bought for any reason, we release the reservation: you
pay nothing at all, and the subscription commitment does not start either.

There are three things worth knowing about the reservation. On Barion's payment page the button reads
**„Pay: …”** — Barion shows the same button for every payment; even then we only
reserve the amount. Your bank may show it in its app as a **pending transaction** —
this is not yet a deduction. And since it is a real card reservation, you can **only pay by bank card**
(not with a Barion balance, Apple Pay or Google Pay).

**Step 3 — Done.** While the amount is only reserved, the tab shows you the steps: amount
reserved → we buy the name → we charge your card. Once the name has been bought and the card charged,
a single sentence at the top of the tab tells you where things stand and when it is expected to finish:
"yourname.com is yours. Your website is expected to be live at the new address by Friday 14:00." Below it are three stages:
**Payment**, **Registration** and **Go live** (under Registration it says ".hu
register" for a `.hu` name and "setting up the address" for any other name). A finished stage is shown in green, the
one in progress with a highlighted frame.

Below it (on a phone) or next to it (on a computer), the **„Details with timestamp”** list shows
every step, with the time next to the finished ones: Paid (for a free address included in your package:
Included in the package) · We bought the name · Registration in the .hu register (only for a
`.hu` name) · The address points to your website · Security certificate · The website at the new address.
From this you can see that the process has not stopped.

You get two emails from us: one when the name is bought ("We have bought your web address", including
what comes next and where your website lives until then), and one when the website is live at the new address.
We charge your card when the name is bought, not at the end of the wait.

For `.hu` names there is an extra step, **Registration**: the screen describes it like this: "The .hu
names are approved by the Registry — we check every 2 minutes". This usually happens within 24 hours,
then a few minutes later your website is live at the new address.

The reason: the Hungarian registry (the organisation that manages `.hu` names) requires a separate
confirmation for every application. **We carry out this step, not you** — the registry writes to our
contact address, because we buy the name on your behalf. So there really is nothing for you
to do; it is just worth knowing that this is why it takes longer.

🛡️ **This is why it matters:** if you do receive an email asking for a "domain confirmation" and
urging you to click a link, it **does not come from us or from the registry** — we never send you
anything like that. Do not click anything in it; forward it to us and we will look into it.

## What if the setup gets stuck?

It can happen that we have already bought the name (and charged your card), but the `.hu`
approval, the address setup or the security certificate takes longer than expected. **The name
is yours even then.** The top of the tab says: "yourname.com is yours, but the setup is taking longer
than expected — our colleague is already on it." (for a `.hu` name: "…but the .hu approval is taking longer
than expected…"), and the delayed stage turns orange. By then the system has already notified
us, our colleague is handling it, and we also tell you by email. There is nothing for you to do, and you do not need to
choose another name or pay again.

## How long does it take, and what happens meanwhile?

For non-Hungarian names (`.com`, `.eu` and similar) it is usually quick: after the name is bought
we set up the address and the security certificate within a few minutes, and your website
moves to the new name. The certificate is what makes the browser show a padlock next to the
address.

For a `.hu` name the registry's approval comes on top of this, which usually happens within 24 hours
— the tab also shows the expected time. Meanwhile your website remains available at its
old address — the move **involves no downtime**.

## Does the old address stop working?

No. The old address automatically redirects to the new one, so business cards and
flyers you have already handed out, and links placed elsewhere, keep working. Google also
transfers to the new address what the old address has built up so far.

## What if someone takes the name in the meantime?

It happens rarely: domain names are sold on a first-come, first-served basis, and a few seconds pass between the check and
the actual purchase. If this happens, the system would rather
stop than buy the wrong name for you.

**In that case you pay nothing.** Since the amount was only reserved, we release the reservation and do not
charge your card. Depending on your bank, it disappears from your account within a few
working days. The subscription commitment does not start either. We tell you on the tab and by email
which name we could not get, and with the **„Choose another name”** button you can
choose another one straight away — the new name you choose takes you to the Review, not back to this
screen.

## How much does it cost?

You always see the price on the **„Overview”** screen before you pay: the address's monthly fee
and the subscription commitment that comes with it. **The fee may depend on the ending** (a `.eu` address
may cost differently from a `.com`) — the Review always shows the fee of the chosen name,
and that is exactly how much we reserve.

The next charge on the Wallet tab and the next invoice on the Modules tab show the amount together with the address's fee,
and the address appears on a separate line among the invoice items. With yearly
payment the address's fee applies for 12 months (the free months of yearly payment apply to our
service, not to the address's fee).

**Your own address has a MONTHLY fee.** The fee appears on your subscription invoice every month,
named on a separate line — there is no large one-off item and no anniversary surprise.
It runs for as long as you keep the name with us: the registry invoices us for the name year after year,
which is why you pay continuously to maintain it.

Three things are worth knowing:

- **Your own address can only be chosen from a certain package size upwards** (with a package of at least a given monthly
  list price) — we state the exact amount on the "Web address" tab. This is an entry condition, not a discount: with a smaller package
  the name is not cheaper, it is unavailable. The condition is decided by the package's **list price**,
  so a temporary discount does not count.
- **No discount applies to the fee.** An introductory or other discount reduces the price of our
  service; the name's fee is a cost paid to the registry and passed on, which is why it always appears in full.
- **Once the minimum term has ended, there is no longer any penalty or package minimum.** The monthly fee
  continues for as long as you keep the name with us. If you cancel, the name becomes yours without a purchase price;
  if you cancel during the minimum term, you can take the name with you by paying the purchase price.

## If my package includes my own address

In some packages your own address is part of the package: then it has no separate monthly fee. If you later
switch to a smaller package, the fee starts — the Modules and Wallet tabs show this in advance, with the
exact monthly amount. On the Web address tab, below the list of names, you also read:
"The name is part of the package, it has no separate fee." — followed by the name's monthly fee with a smaller package:
the fee of the selected name's ending, or, while no name is selected, the fee range of the endings.
If you select another name, the amount adjusts to its ending. If you request such a free address later, for a website that is already live, the
Review shows this in place of the address's fee: "included in the package · 12-month minimum term" (the number of months
depends on your package). You pay no fee and we reserve nothing, but requesting the address starts
the minimum term — its conditions are described above, in the "How much does it cost?" section. When you click the **„I'd like this”** (I want this one)
button, we buy the name immediately, and the tab shows the process in the same way
as for a paid name. We let you know by email as soon as the address is live.

After the click, the button's label changes to: "Checking the name once more…" — wait,
do not press it again. If you see this in the same place: "The request could not be started.
Please try again.", click the **„I'd like this”** (I want this one) button again.

If we still cannot buy the name (for example someone else reserved it in the meantime), the tab says so,
and you can choose another name in the same place. In that case you have not paid anything either, and the minimum term has not
started. Only one such name can be requested at a time: while one is in progress or live, the tab
shows that one.

## If I already have my own domain

If you bought a name elsewhere earlier, it can also be connected to your website, but this is not yet
self-service. Write to us and we will take care of it.
